newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds received a fillip towards the close on Thursday after a surge in U.S. Treasuries prompted by weaker-than-expected retail sales figures.
"Movement-wise it was dead, range-trading stuff today. The only thing that seemed to get people excited was the (U.S.) numbers," said one bond dealer.
The benchmark R150 was taken from its intraday high of 14.70 percent to lie in line with Wednesday's 1400 GMT level of 14.645 percent toward the close.
While some dealers said volumes were lacking, others said eurorand hedging, switch trades and possibly asset swap activity had actually swelled turnover.
The late recovery was unlikely to continue for long, players warned, with the market generally seen near its capacity to absorb stock and spoiling for a test of the upside ceiling of 14.69 percent.
"I get the impresion that everyone's got stocked to the gills and they're feeling a little bit puffy so we might not break the downside and return to the upside in the near term," said one trader.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 7.44 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.12 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates were static at 16.05 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate remained pegged at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent also unchanged from Wednesday.
Foreigners were net sellers of 2.05 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 540.92 million rands worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes rose to 5.71 billion rand on Wednesday from 4.99 billion rand previously.
